cards.title: Why Child's 'Na-na-na' Sounds So Annoying
cards.body: A Guardian reader series explores why repetitive sounds from children trigger such strong parental reactions. Understanding the psychology behind childhood behavior helps parents respond with patience.

cards.title: Managing Partner's Behavior at Kids' Sports
cards.body: When a partner acts inappropriately at children's football matches, it can strain relationships and embarrass kids. Communication and understanding the root of anger are key to resolving the conflict.

cards.title: Human Connection Matters More Than Tech Fears
cards.body: A pediatrician argues that loss of human connection—not screens—poses the biggest threat to children's wellbeing. Open communication with kids remains the most effective parenting tool.

cards.title: Halloween Magic for Families This Year
cards.body: Celebrating autumn traditions like Halloween creates meaningful moments and connection with children. Embracing seasonal activities brings magic and joy to family life.

cards.title: ADHD in Women Often Goes Undiagnosed
cards.body: ADHD symptoms in women appear as overwhelm rather than hyperactivity and often overlap with anxiety or depression. Early recognition helps mothers get proper support and treatment.

cards.title: Understanding Your Partner's Attachment Style
cards.body: Knowing your partner's attachment style prevents misinterpreting their behavior and strengthens your relationship. This awareness is crucial for creating a stable home environment for children.

cards.title: Teen Mental Health Beyond Screens
cards.body: Research shows we may be focusing too narrowly on screen time when addressing teen mental health. A broader approach to understanding adolescent wellbeing is needed.
